root_cause.text: The drm/xe GuC submission path incorrectly optimized suspend for idle non-parallel exec queues by skipping schedule toggling/GuC suspend, which in LR/preempt-fence VM mode prevented the required context switch that flushes TLB entries for invalidated userptr VMAs.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit message explicitly states that the “idle-skip optimization bypasses GuC suspend, so the GPU may not perform the context switch that flushes TLB entries for invalidated userptr VMAs,” and the patch removes `xe_exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend()`, the `EXEC_QUEUE_STATE_IDLE_SKIP_SUSPEND` state, and restores unconditional suspend/resume scheduling logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the inline xe_exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend() helper and its documentation, leaving callers to use the underlying queue state checks directly.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the entire static inline function xe_exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend() and its associated kernel-doc comment from the header file, deleting the helper that returned !xe_exec_queue_is_parallel(q) && xe_exec_queue_is_idle(q).
intent_record.how: This change eliminates a convenience wrapper for checking whether an exec queue can skip suspend handling; any code that used this helper must now stop using it or perform the underlying checks directly, with no new runtime behavior introduced by this hunk alone.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused exec queue idle-skip-suspend state flag definition from the exec queue state bitmask declarations.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the preprocessor macro definition `#define EXEC_QUEUE_STATE_IDLE_SKIP_SUSPEND (1 << 11)` from the exec queue state flag declarations, leaving the surrounding state bit definitions unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this eliminates the named state flag from the code so it can no longer be referenced as a distinct exec queue state bit; this suggests the idle-skip-suspend state is being retired or was unused, reducing the set of defined exec queue states without adding new behavior in this hunk.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant helper wrappers for the EXEC_QUEUE_STATE_IDLE_SKIP_SUSPEND state bit.
intent_record.what: Three static helper functions were removed: one that tested whether q->guc->state contains EXEC_QUEUE_STATE_IDLE_SKIP_SUSPEND, one that set that flag with atomic_or(), and one that cleared it with atomic_and().
intent_record.how: This eliminates local wrappers around reading, setting, and clearing the EXEC_QUEUE_STATE_IDLE_SKIP_SUSPEND bit, so any runtime behavior tied to these helpers is no longer provided through these functions; by itself this suggests no direct logic change beyond removing unused or redundant accessors.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always update the ring tail for non-parallel exec queues during submission instead of skipping it based on exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend().
intent_record.what: The conditional branch in submit_exec_queue() was changed by removing the call to exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend(q) from the non-parallel path, replacing `else if (!exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend(q))` with an unconditional `else` before calling `xe_lrc_set_ring_tail(lrc, lrc->ring.tail)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, non-parallel execution queues will now always update the LRC ring tail during this path instead of conditionally skipping the update when exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend(q) returned true. This ensures the ring tail is consistently submitted for eligible jobs and avoids suppressing queue submission state updates based on the idle-skip-suspend check.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the idle-skip-suspend exclusion so valid exec queues still go through normal suspend processing.
intent_record.what: The local boolean variable `idle_skip_suspend`, initialized from `xe_exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend(q)`, was removed, and the suspend-processing `if` condition was simplified by deleting the `!idle_skip_suspend &&` check while keeping the existing state-change, suspended, and enabled checks.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the suspend-processing path will now execute for eligible exec queues regardless of whether `xe_exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend(q)` would have returned true, so queues previously excluded by the idle-skip-suspend condition can now enter the wait/suspend handling logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused sched_context helper that directly issued GuC SCHED_CONTEXT requests and updated the LRC tail.
intent_record.what: The change removes the entire static function sched_context(struct xe_exec_queue *q), including its local variable setup, runtime assertions, trace call, ring tail update via xe_lrc_set_ring_tail(), and the xe_guc_ct_send() call that issued XE_GUC_ACTION_SCHED_CONTEXT for the queue.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this eliminates the code path that explicitly scheduled a GuC context by sending a SCHED_CONTEXT action and updating the LRC ring tail from this helper. Any behavior that depended on invoking this helper is removed, meaning scheduling/resume handling will no longer perform this direct context submission through this function.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove incorrect idle-skip-suspend handling from exec queue resume processing so resume only performs normal state transitions.
intent_record.what: The change removes all handling of the exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend(q) condition from __guc_exec_queue_process_msg_resume(). Specifically, it deletes the branch that, when the queue was not enabled, cleared the idle-skip-suspend flag and updated the LRC ring tail; deletes the else-if branch that, when the queue was enabled, cleared the flag and called sched_context(q); and also deletes clearing of the idle-skip-suspend flag from the fallback else path.
intent_record.how: At runtime, resume message processing no longer performs any special-case work for queues marked with the idle-skip-suspend state. Resuming now only clears the suspended state and, for disabled queues, marks resume pending and enables scheduling. This prevents the resume path from resetting the idle-skip-suspend flag, touching the ring tail, or forcing a scheduling context operation during resume processing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always suspend fault-mode LR queues and require retry when dependencies exist, removing the idle-based skip path and its related accounting.
intent_record.what: The change removes the local variable `idle_skip_suspend`, deletes the call to `xe_exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend(q)`, removes the conditional `if (!idle_skip_suspend && has_deps)` in favor of `if (has_deps)`, deletes the conditional stats increment for `XE_GT_STATS_ID_HW_ENGINE_GROUP_SKIP_LR_QUEUE_COUNT`, and replaces `need_resume |= !idle_skip_suspend;` with unconditional `need_resume = true;` before calling `q->ops->suspend(q)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, fault-mode exec queues in the group are no longer allowed to bypass suspend based on idle state. If dependencies exist, the function now always returns `-EAGAIN` for such queues, and every processed fault-mode queue is treated as needing resume and is suspended unconditionally. This also stops reporting skipped suspend statistics for idle queues.

Remove the idle-based skip-suspend path from exec queue submission/suspend/resume handling so fault-mode LR queues always follow normal suspend behavior and retry when dependencies exist.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability was caused by the idle-skip-suspend optimization for non-parallel exec queues. This group removes the helper/API and associated state flag for that idle-skip-suspend path, directly eliminating the mechanism tied to the root cause rather than making an unrelated refactor.

The changes directly remove the idle-based skip-suspend optimization in GuC exec queue submit/suspend/resume paths, which is the stated root cause preventing the suspend/context-switch behavior needed to flush TLBs for invalidated userptr VMAs in LR/preempt-fence VM mode.

This change removes an unused helper for direct GuC SCHED_CONTEXT requests and LRC tail updates, but the vulnerability was caused by suspend-path optimization skipping schedule toggling/GuC suspend needed to force a context switch and TLB flush. Removing an unused helper does not address that root cause.

candidates.rationale: This conditional explicitly excluded idle non-parallel queues from normal suspend handling, embodying the optimization that skipped the suspend path and thus could avoid the context switch needed to flush invalidated userptr TLB entries in fault-mode LR/preempt-fence VM mode.

By only retrying when dependencies existed for queues not marked idle-skip-suspend, this statement let idle queues bypass the required suspend/retry flow in fault-mode LR handling, contributing directly to the incorrect suspend optimization.
This line encoded that idle-skip-suspend queues did not need the normal suspend/resume cycle, which is the core faulty assumption behind missing the context switch/TLB flush.

This helper defined the vulnerable policy itself: any non-parallel idle queue could skip suspend. That logic is the root cause because fault-mode LR/preempt-fence VM queues still required suspend/context-switch behavior even when idle.

This condition skipped ring-tail update for idle-skip-suspend queues during submission, part of the broader optimization path that avoided normal queue state transitions associated with the necessary context switch.

vuln_statements.explanation: This helper encodes the flawed policy at the root of the vulnerability: treating any non-parallel idle exec queue as eligible to skip suspend. In LR/preempt-fence VM mode, even idle queues still needed the suspend/context-switch path to flush invalidated userptr TLB entries.

This condition explicitly excluded idle-skip-suspend queues from normal suspend state handling. That exclusion is the direct manifestation of the buggy optimization that prevented the required suspend/context-switch sequence needed for TLB flushes.

This line records that idle-skip-suspend queues do not require the suspend/resume cycle. That assumption is precisely what caused fault-mode LR queues to miss the context switch required to flush invalidated userptr mappings.

By gating dependency-triggered suspend/retry behavior on !idle_skip_suspend, this statement allowed idle queues to bypass the suspend flow in fault-mode LR handling, contributing to the missing context switch/TLB flush.

This branch skipped ring-tail update behavior for queues classified as idle-skip-suspend, reinforcing the broader optimization path that avoided normal submission/suspend handling associated with the required context switch.
